transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Recording: (auto) Fireflies recording link omitted
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Obsidian Head of Partnerships), Ethan Lowe (Obsidian Cloud Ops), Samir Patel (Obsidian BizDev)

Summary:
Quick intro call to explore an affiliate / reseller partnership between Redwood Inference and Obsidian AI (Obsidian provides a GPU-first cloud with reseller channels). Focus on integration points: Dedicated and private deployment options, VPC peering, partner billing/rev-share, co-marketing, and a small technical compatibility check for GPU SKUs and driver stacks.

Topics covered (brief):
- Partnership model (affiliate vs reseller vs OEM)
- Technical compatibility (GPU families, NVLink, quantization, container images)
- Security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS)
- Pilot/PoC scope and benchmarks (throughput/latency targets)
- Commercial cadence (rev-share, credits, lead flow)

Transcript (selected excerpts, auto timestamps):
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour so we'll try to keep to the agenda. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. Diego, SE, will cover tech bits.
[00:18] Priya Malhotra: Thanks Maya, excited to chat, Obsidian runs a couple of GPU clusters and we're exploring affiliate partnerships to resell inference services.
[00:29] Diego Alvarez: Great. Quick intro, at Redwood we run hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so depending on how you want to position customers we can do a hosted endpoint with referral credits, or dedicated pools for Obsidian-managed customers, or a private VPC option.
[00:52] Samir Patel: When you say private VPC option, is that like VPC peering or do you ship a package for on-prem?
[01:03] Diego Alvarez: Good question — both. We have a Redwood Private package that can be deployed into a customer VPC or private datacenter; for cloud partners the common pattern is VPC peering and shared control plane, or a managed private control plane that lives in Obsidian's account.
[01:25] Ethan Lowe: From Ops perspective we need to know what network ports, encryption, and peering requirements you have; we also care about billing model — metered tokens vs flat committed capacity.
[01:41] Maya Chen: Totally. For affiliates we'd usually do a referral credit model initially — simple rev-share on usage — and for bigger customers Obsidian could resell dedicated capacity with a committed monthly minimum.
[01:58] Priya Malhotra: How do you handle model licensing? Some of our enterprise customers want specific model variants and licensed weights.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: We have a model catalog and we support pinned model versions. For licensed weights you'd typically arrange license terms — Redwood can host licensed models in Private mode so the customer keys the model and we serve it in a compliant environment. There's some nuance with EULAs for commercial weights.
[02:34] Samir Patel: Ok. Can you support quantized models? Our price-sensitive customers like 4-bit quantized variants.
[02:44] Diego Alvarez: Yes, our runtime supports int8 and 4-bit paths for many architectures; compatibility depends on the backend kernels and the exact model. We'll run a quick compatibility checklist against your instance SKUs.
[02:58] Priya Malhotra: Great. On the commercial side, what's the normal rev-share split for affiliates?
[03:05] Maya Chen: It varies — early affiliate pilots tend to be 10-25% of net revenue, with higher tiers for committed resellers; we can share a one-pager with ranges and a partner portal mockup.
[03:18] Ethan Lowe: Network security — do you need cross-account IAM roles? Are there logs that land in our account?
[03:29] Diego Alvarez: For VPC peering flows, we usually keep runtime in Redwood but we can ship logs to your S3 or object storage via cross-account role, and we support customer-managed KMS for keying. If you want the private control plane in your account, audit logs live in your environment.
[03:47] Priya Malhotra: SOC2 and ISO — do you have those? Some of our customers require that as a checkbox.
[03:55] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant and we can share the auditor report under NDA. We also have SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, and detailed audit logs.
[04:07] Samir Patel: Who would own first-line support for co-sold customers?
[04:12] Maya Chen: We typically do joint support — level 1 is the reseller, level 2 Redwood. For early pilots we can do white-glove support with a shared contact list.
[04:21] Priya Malhotra: Ok sounds fair.
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: Tech deep-dive item: NVLink and multi-GPU scaling — if Obsidian exposes HVX / NVLink aware instances we can take advantage for large context models, otherwise we'll fallback to multi-host sharding which impacts latency.
[04:45] Ethan Lowe: Our fleet includes A100 and H100s with NVLink in the DGX-style nodes and smaller VMs without NVLink. Is there a material perf difference?
[04:57] Diego Alvarez: Yes — NVLink with contiguous memory lets us keep KV caches and large activations local; without it there's extra cross-host comms. For low-latency short-chat workloads smaller VMs are fine; for long-context or huge batches H100 with NVLink gives big gains.
[05:18] Priya Malhotra: Do you require a specific container runtime or driver versions? We manage drivers centrally and upgrades are slow.
[05:28] Diego Alvarez: We provide validated container images and matrix of driver+OS combos we support. Most customers run NGC driver sets; we can accept custom drivers but there's extra validation. I'll send a compatibility table.
[05:39] Samir Patel: What's the onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[05:44] Maya Chen: For a small affiliate pilot it's usually 2-4 weeks: paperwork and rev-share terms 1 week, technical integration (VPC peering / access) 1-2 weeks, then a short bench / acceptance. If you want dedicated capacity or private control plane could be 4-8 weeks.
[06:01] Ethan Lowe: Benchmarks — what do you need from us to run a performance test?
[06:07] Diego Alvarez: We’d like: a sample model or family, typical seq lengths, expected qps, and instance SKUs; we'll run throughput/latency runs and share a report. Also a traffic profile — bursty vs steady.
[06:23] Priya Malhotra: On lead flow — can we get a portal or API? We have partners who want direct conversion tracking.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Yes we have a partner portal planned — for early pilots we'll do CSV/Salesforce flows, later we'll integrate lead API. We can also provide co-branded landing pages and trial credits.
[06:44] Samir Patel: Any exclusivity or territory models? Some partners want exclusive APAC rights.
[06:50] Maya Chen: We typically avoid strict exclusivity unless there's a big commitment; we can do prioritized support or preferred pricing for strategic partners.
[06:59] Priya Malhotra: Compliance customers will ask about data residency — can you keep logs in specific regions?
[07:07] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support regional pinning for hosted offerings and allow log retention in customer-chosen regions for Private deployments.
[07:16] Ethan Lowe: A couple of specific tech constraints: our internal networking blocks outbound 9000-9100 ports by default for security; do you use those?
[07:26] Diego Alvarez: Our default gRPC ports are around 8500-8600, but we can map ports and work with your firewall team. We'll need a small set of ports for control plane and tunnel handshake.
[07:38] Priya Malhotra: Do you have any partner references we could speak to?
[07:42] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a couple of cloud partners and channel resellers — I'll share anonymized references and a case study.
[07:49] Samir Patel: Pricing: Are there partner discounts or commit credits?
[07:53] Maya Chen: For affiliates there's usually startup credits and then a rev-share; for resellers with commits we offer tiered discounts. Details in the one-pager.
[08:02] Ethan Lowe: Driver versions — if we can't upgrade right away, will that block a PoC?
[08:08] Diego Alvarez: It can but often we can run a compatible kernel with fallbacks; sometimes quantized kernels need specific drivers — that's why we want to run a quick compatibility checklist.
[08:19] Priya Malhotra: Ok let's talk pilots. We're thinking of offering 3 customers for a co-sell pilot — medium enterprise with latency sensitivity and another two smaller.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Sounds great. For the latency-sensitive one we'd probably propose a dedicated pool or Private in your account; for the small ones hosted with credits is simpler.
[08:41] Ethan Lowe: Are there throttles or QoS primitives we can expose to customers?
[08:46] Diego Alvarez: Yes — per-route throttles, quotas, and model-level priority lanes. We can map to your product catalog.
[08:55] Samir Patel: Integrations: Do you expose a REST API or only SDKs?
[08:59] Maya Chen: Both — REST + SDKs (Python/JS/Go). We also have streaming and function/tool calling patterns.
[09:08] Priya Malhotra: Marketing: what's co-marketing look like? Joint webinars, PR?
[09:12] Maya Chen: Typical: co-branded webinars, joint blog posts, sales enablement packs, and listing in our partner directory. Early partners get feature placement.
[09:21] Ethan Lowe: Ok — on the technical checklist, Samir and I will share the instance SKU matrix and network topology.
[09:28] Priya Malhotra: We'll need legal templates for a reseller agreement to review.
[09:33] Maya Chen: We'll share a partner MSA draft and the one-pager.
[09:37] Diego Alvarez: Quick note: model artifacts — if you want us to bring a model into a Private environment, we need the model weights or a link to a licensed registry. Some registries have pull-rate limits.
[09:50] Samir Patel: Are there usage reporting dashboards for partners?
[09:55] Maya Chen: Yes — in Redwood Console partners can view token-level cost, route breakdown, and per-customer dashboards; we can give view-only partner roles.
[10:06] Priya Malhotra: Support SLAs? We have enterprise customers that need 2-hour incident ack.
[10:12] Maya Chen: We offer premium SLA add-ons — 1-hour or 2-hour acknowledgements depending on tier. We'll log those in the SOW.
[10:20] Ethan Lowe: Any hidden costs — ingress, egress, model storage?
[10:24] Maya Chen: Clear line items — token usage, embedding costs, storage costs for pinned models, and optional dedicated capacity fees. We'll outline in the commercial one-pager.
[10:34] Diego Alvarez: A technical gotcha: KV cache warming during model switchovers can cause a small latency spike; we have strategies for pre-warm and graceful fallback.
[10:44] Priya Malhotra: Good to know.
[10:48] Samir Patel: Timeline: if we start paperwork next week, when could the pilot start?
[10:54] Maya Chen: If we do paperwork and credits this week, and tech integration next 2 weeks, pilot could kick off in 2-3 weeks.
[11:05] Priya Malhotra: Ok that's reasonable. Anything else on the tech side, Ethan?
[11:10] Ethan Lowe: One more — GPU firmware levels, do you require specific firmware?
[11:14] Diego Alvarez: Not usually but for specific features like MIG or some H100 capabilities firmware matters; we'll add that to the matrix.
[11:23] Maya Chen: Alright let's recap next steps: we'll send the partner one-pager, rev-share ranges, sample partner MSA, Diego will send compatibility checklist, and Obsidian will send instance SKUs and network topology.
[11:37] Priya Malhotra: Sounds good — we'll aim to get those items to you early next week.
[11:44] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[11:47] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the tech sync.
[11:56] (call ends)
